key_insight: A neural network potential trained on ab initio data can accurately model oxygen-vacancy formation and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3 at scales unreachable by direct DFT molecular dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical prediction of defect-driven transport in perovskite oxides, supporting more reliable materials design for oxide electronics and related energy devices.
method: Generated a reference dataset from AIMD/DFT simulations of pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Trained an NNP to reproduce energies, forces, and virials, including vacancy supercell-size effects.
Ran large-scale NNP-MD and fitted an Arrhenius relation to extract vacancy migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP matched DFT reference properties and yielded vacancy diffusion coefficients and a 0.64 eV migration enthalpy in close agreement with the experimental 0.67 eV value.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the coverage and quality of the AIMD training data, so unseen defect environments or extreme conditions may require retraining or additional validation.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
